deities: Lord Vishnu as Sundarnarayan (presiding deity, in the sanctum)
Goddess Lakshmi (flanking Vishnu in the sanctum)
Goddess Saraswati (flanking Vishnu in the sanctum)
Hanuman, Narayana and Indra (carvings on the temple walls)
festivals: Annual equinox event on 21st March (the rising sun's first rays fall directly on the idols; draws thousands of devotees)

history.dynasty: Maratha period (Peshwa era); built by Gangadhar Yashwant Chandrachud
history.summary: The Sundarnarayan Temple, a Vaishnavite shrine on the lofty west bank of the Godavari at Panchavati, Nashik, was built in 1756 by Gangadhar Yashwant Chandrachud, a Maratha chieftain of the Peshwa era. Legend says Lord Vishnu took the form of Sundarnarayan and bathed in the sacred water tank on the Godavari here; after regaining his original form he was called Sundarnarayan, and the Badarika Sangam pond still lies on the road leading to the river. The east-facing temple is a finely carved stone structure with three porches, balcony seating, lobed arches, globular domes and a vaulted niche showing Mughal influence. Its most remarkable feature is its orientation: on 21st March (the spring equinox) the rays of the rising sun fall exactly upon the idols, an event witnessed by thousands of devotees each year. The temple is managed by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI); recent reports note it has been undergoing conservation/restoration work (verify current status before visiting).

name: Sundarnarayan Temple
town_description: Nashik (Nasik), on the banks of the Godavari in northern Maharashtra, is one of India's ancient pilgrimage cities, associated with the Ramayana - Panchavati on the river's north bank is where Rama, Sita and Lakshmana are said to have stayed during their exile. It is famed for its 200 temples and bathing ghats, the Kumbh Mela (held at Nashik-Trimbakeshwar every 12 years), and the nearby Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga. Nashik is also India's wine capital and a major industrial city, about 180 km northeast of Mumbai.

travel.airport: Ojhar (Ozar) Nashik International Airport (approx. 24 km); Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport (approx. 136-180 km) is the nearest major airport.
travel.railway: Nashik Road Railway Station (NK, approx. 9-10 km from Panchavati), well connected to Mumbai, Pune, Delhi and other major cities.
travel.road: In Panchavati near the Ahilyabai Holkar Bridge, about 2 km from Nashik Central Bus Station; autos, taxis and city buses run from the station and city centre. Nashik is approx. 180 km from Mumbai by road (4-5 hours).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. 21st March is the most special day to visit (equinox sun-ray event) but draws large crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 6:00 AM to 12:00 noon; evening 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM, open all days (verify - some listings show 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM or 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM, possibly during restoration). Entry is free. Dress modestly (avoid shorts, tank tops and exposed legs). The temple has been reported under restoration with main deities shifted to an adjacent worship area (verify before visiting).
